confidence_semantics: publisher/source authority only; not parcel numeric accuracy

candidates.name: National Polygon Service
verified_facts: HMLR describes National Polygon Service as licensed chargeable datasets including National Polygon, Title Descriptor and Title Number/UPRN lookup.
National Polygon geometry is described as indicative shape and position of registered-title boundaries and the service is updated monthly.
semantic_limits: Paid National Polygon Service is not a required dependency for this AAYS workflow while free official INSPIRE discovery geometry exists.
Paid status or richer attributes do not make index polygons exact legal boundaries or terrain measurements.

candidates.name: Electronic extent data (polygons)
verified_facts: HMLR electronic extent services provide requested registered-title polygons for use in GIS and can supply open-standard GIS files.
The service is a spatial/property information product rather than an elevation dataset.
semantic_limits: Polygon delivery format does not establish legal-boundary precision beyond the source product semantics.
Extent data cannot be used as terrain-height evidence.

candidates.name: Geospatial Data Catalogue: HM Land Registry
verified_facts: The official catalogue indexes location-linked electronic datasets held by HM Land Registry.
The catalogue itself is OGL, while underlying datasets can use different licences.
semantic_limits: Catalogue presence is discovery/provenance evidence only.
Catalogue licensing does not establish polygon accuracy or elevation confidence.

candidates.name: Geospatial Data Catalogue CSV preview
verified_facts: The catalogue describes Index Map polygons as captured against OS MasterMap at typical urban, rural and mountain/moorland mapping scales.
It explicitly describes index-polygon extents as indicative and says Title Plan and Title Register should be consulted for full details.
semantic_limits: Map capture scale is horizontal cartographic context, not vertical terrain accuracy.
Indicative index polygon geometry must remain separate from determined-boundary evidence.

candidates.publisher: HM Land Registry / National Data Library
candidates.name: Geospatial Data Catalogue mirror
verified_facts: The National Data Library mirror identifies HM Land Registry as publisher and was updated 8 July 2026.
It describes the catalogue as core metadata about geospatial datasets and notes underlying datasets may have different licences.
semantic_limits: Fresh catalogue metadata is not parcel geometry or elevation measurement evidence.

candidates.name: Datum, ellipsoid and projection information
verified_facts: OS lists EPSG:27700 for OSGB36 2D National Grid and EPSG:7405 for the 3D National Grid plus ODN height compound CRS.
The same reference distinguishes ODN vertical datum and OSGM15 transformation identifiers from horizontal CRS identifiers.
semantic_limits: CRS identifiers define reference systems; they do not prove which transformation was applied to a specific EA survey.
Horizontal and vertical CRS semantics must remain separate.

candidates.name: Types of coordinates
verified_facts: OS distinguishes ellipsoid height from orthometric/geoid height and explains why ellipsoid distance is not equivalent to height above a level surface.
Orthometric height is referenced to the geoid so relative height better represents physical gradient.
semantic_limits: A conceptual height definition is not evidence of a parcel-specific survey transformation or accuracy.

candidates.name: Ordnance Survey coordinate systems
verified_facts: OS identifies National Grid/OSGB36 as the traditional horizontal coordinate system and ODN as the traditional vertical coordinate system for Britain.
OS Net provides a modern 3D framework from which National Grid and ODN coordinates are obtained using transformations.
semantic_limits: National coordinate-system architecture does not replace exact EA survey metadata lineage.

candidates.name: Guide to Coordinate Systems in Great Britain
verified_facts: The current OS guide routes users through coordinate types, OS coordinate systems, geodetic transformations and datum/projection references.
The guide explicitly treats mean-sea-level/orthometric height and ellipsoid height as different concepts requiring appropriate transformations.
semantic_limits: Guide routing is reference/provenance evidence, not a parcel observation.
